items.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby's grandfather thanks community, says time to 'let justice take its course'
items.description: The family of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby, whose body was found on the outskirts of Alice Springs on Thursday, has thanked the community for their support as tributes flow in from across the country.

items.title: Police pulled him over on his farm. He was tasered 30 seconds later
items.description: Disturbing cases of people wrongly tasered by police on their farm and at school has raised questions over whether officers are too reliant on the devices.

items.title: Brisbane Lions coach slams 'hero' parent after whiteboard leak
items.description: Chris Fagan has expressed his disappointment after the leaking of confidential Brisbane Lions notes on Essendon players.

items.title: Live: Saints onslaught stuns Blues after towering mark ignites blustery clash
items.description: Matthew Carroll soars for Carlton in a spiteful clash with St Kilda, after Richmond snapped a 12-game winless run with victory against West Coast. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Broncos fall short of miracle comeback as Reynolds hurt again
items.description: As the Broncos welcome back Reece Walsh and Pat Carrigan, the Roosters give Cody Ramsey his first NRL minutes since 2022. Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: Liberal Party retains the seat of Nepean in by-election
items.description: Anthony Marsh wins the Nepean by-election, retaining the seat for the Liberal Party.

items.title: How a 'loner' went from a life of privilege to Bondi gunman
items.description: Sajid Akram was a man of unusual secrecy — even to his own family. New details uncovered by Background Briefing shed light on his downward spiral into violence.

items.title: Israeli police video shows attack on nun in Jerusalem
items.description: Israeli police release a video showing what eyewitnesses say was an attack by a Jewish man on a nun near Jerusalem's Old City. Police say the suspect, a 36-year-old man, was later arrested.

items.title: Who's really in charge in Iran?
items.description: There's growing belief it's not the supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei but Ahmad Vahidi, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps boss and ideological hardliner. So are the generals really in charge in Iran?

items.title: US to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany amid Trump spat with Merz
items.description: The United States is withdrawing 5,000 troops from NATO ally Germany amid a growing a rift between the nations' leaders over the Iran war.

items.title: Second of two new Spirit of Tasmania ferries arrives in Geelong
items.description: Following a seven-week journey from Scotland, the Spirit of Tasmania V has arrived in Geelong. It will undergo gantry testing tomorrow before being temporarily relocated to Station Pier in Melbourne.

items.title: Polar blast and snow to follow record May heat over south-east Australia
items.description: Just weeks from winter, and south-east Australia is still enjoying summertime warmth.

items.title: Why this cattle farmer is flooding his property with salt water
items.description: More than half a century ago, lush wetlands along the Queensland coastline were cut off from the ocean as farmers built physical barriers to stop salt water flowing into their land. Now, conservation groups and traditional owners are restoring tidal flows and bringing life back to the land.

items.title: Sabotage and violence alleged on major Brisbane rail project
items.description: Queensland's inquiry into the CFMEU has revealed Cross River Rail was plagued by years of interference. Here are the key takeaways from this week's hearings.

items.title: Why Dee Salmin thinks her book could end relationships
items.description: Podcaster Dee Salmin says people should steer clear of traditional dating advice and focus more on themselves.

items.title: 1976 in music: The big albums turning 50 this year
items.description: The music industry is always in a state of flux, but what was happening in 1976 was akin to the dinosaurs looking up and seeing a meteor on the way.

items.title: This pumpkin soup is comfort food with a twist that takes it to the next level
items.description: Pumpkin soup is one of a few meals with just one main ingredient. This delicious version spices things up with coconut cream and an easy curry-leaf oil.

items.title: Gas vs beer: How Pocock caused the government a tax headache
items.description: David Pocock was struggling to find cut-through on the issue of gas taxes, but then a question about the beer excise sparked a social media war of words.

items.title: The four women who left 'Australia Street' to try and leave Syria
items.description: Four Australian women, their children and grandchildren are stuck in limbo in Syria after leaving a refugee camp for family members of suspected Islamic State fighters. This is what we know about them.

items.title: Shift in the Middle East has implications for countries like Australia
items.description: Donald Trump's earlier signalling that he will neither walk away from the war declaring a victory or escalate it, but will try to starve the Iranians out, suggests there is no clear sign of how this war could end.

items.title: Iran's race: Break the US blockade or risk its economic lifeline
items.description: Analysis of how much oil Iran is producing, shipping and having to store shows pressure is mounting on Tehran, but while experts agree the US blockade is effective, there are questions about whether it can really force Iran back to the negotiating table.

items.title: As I sat for an Archibald entry, I tried to assume an air of dignity
items.description: What began as an awkward pose for the Archibald Prize became a meditation on why portrait painting still matters in the age of the iPhone.

items.title: Cosmetics will soon cost more. Here's why
items.description: Australians spend about $450 on average on beauty products per year. That could soon rise as petroleum prices increase.

items.title: Fiji considers state of emergency after suspected drug kingpin murder in custody
items.description: The suspected murder of a Fijian underworld figure held in military custody has sparked a new chapter in the island nation's wrestle with drug-related crimes, with the police and military combining forces for a highly visible "crackdown".

items.title: What is a town camp and what is life like there for Aboriginal people?
items.description: Kumanjayi Little Baby is believed to have been taken from her bed at night while visiting a town camp near Alice Springs with her mother. This is how town camps came to be.
